title: Measures for Prompt Police Case Resolution and Mandating Assignment of Police Officers with Child Protection Training in Child-related Cases
what_it_is: Measures for Prompt Police Case Resolution and Mandating Assignment of Police Officers with Child Protection Training in Child-related Cases

sections.label: Fatal child abuse case questions
sections.summary: Questions ask why a missing child report was classified low-risk and how risk guidelines and supervision will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs on the February 2020 fatal child abuse case (a) why did the Investigation Officer classify the missing child report as low-risk; (b) what steps will the Ministry take to review the risk classification guidelines and follow-up requirements for Investigation Officers’ use especially for cases of missing vulnerable persons; and (c) how will supervision of Investigation Officers be strengthened.

sections.label: Investigation Officer escalation failure
sections.summary: The Investigation Officer and her supervisor failed to follow Police procedures to escalate the case to regular case review sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Investigation Officer (IO) who dealt with the first Police report, and her supervisor, failed to follow Police's procedures to escalate the case to the regular case review sessions for monitoring and guidance.

sections.label: Police discipline of officer
sections.summary: Police began internal investigations in 2020 and disciplined both the Investigation Officer and her supervisor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Police commenced internal investigations once the case came to light in 2020, and disciplined both the IO and her supervisor.

sections.label: Police family violence training and teams
sections.summary: In 2022 Police introduced a Family Violence Training Package, and in 2023 formed Family Violence Teams at all Land Divisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In 2022, they introduced the Family Violence Training Package for all frontline and IOs to adopt a sensitive approach to family violence cases, including child abuse cases, and to recognise and escalate and work high-risk cases together with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In 2023, the Police formed Family Violence Teams (FVTs) at all Land Divisions to give focus to family violence cases, including child abuse cases.

sections.label: Timeline of independent review decision
sections.summary: A question asks how the decision to independently review Megan's case was made only after MSF's 8 April 2025 statement.

sentences.speaker: (Resumption for supplementary questions)
sentences.text: The decision was taken after MSF's first statement on the case on 8 April 2025, so may I seek the Minister's clarifications on the timeline and how the decision to independently review Megan's case was made only after 8 April 2025?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: I mentioned in my response that for Child Protection Service, now known as Protective Service, we have doubled our Child Protection Officers from 45 in 2019, to more than 90 in 2040, and we are continuing to expand.

sections.label: Independent Panel after new information
sections.summary: MSF convened an independent Panel after new information surfaced in 2025, despite earlier internal reviews and bilaterals.

sentences.text: I think Minister Masagos, as well as MSF had explained previously that in 2020, internal reviews had been carried out by the organisations concerned as well as bilaterals with MSF.

But in 2025, both during and after the sentencing of the perpetrators involved in Megan's death, new information had surfaced, for example, photographs as well as new information from some of the agencies concerned.
And MSF decided, notwithstanding the bilaterals done earlier, to convene an independent Panel, in order to strengthen the safeguards in our system and to look into the new facts that have surfaced.

sections.label: Apology for misunderstanding
sections.summary: The speaker says they have read the report and apologised to relevant agencies, including Beyond Social Services, for the misunderstanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And we have read the report and seen what happened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, to the extent that there was a misunderstanding that there was finger pointing, we have apologised to the relevant agencies, including Beyond Social Services, for the misunderstanding that had occurred.

sections.label: Sector Specific Screening Guide
sections.summary: The Sector Specific Screening Guide trains frontliners, including preschools, to assess cases of concern and report them for closer look.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They come to school every day, or almost every day, and you want to maintain that relationship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, with the Sectors Specific Screening Guide, which we endeavour to train and have been training many frontliners, including in the preschools, it gives them some guide to look at in order to assess whether this is a case of concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: No doubt, concerned teachers and school leaders will ask questions, will show concern, and that is the right thing to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But when enough of the dots are connected and you see that in the Sector Specific Screening Guide, then, the guidance to our agencies and preschools is: report; have this looked at more closely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The third question that the Member has is initiatives like the one he mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We welcome community organisations, even corporates who want to play a part in strengthening public education, strengthening awareness and helping in this collective effort to look out for the vulnerable amongst us, whether it is children, persons with disability, seniors, and so on.

sections.label: UK department and audit questions
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Ministry will study similar jurisdictions and set timelines, audit and public reporting for enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is a non-ministerial department of the government of UK, but it reports directly to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, my first supplementary question to the Minister is this: in next year's review, would the Ministry also study similar jurisdictions and approaches to further strengthen accountability and coordination in our child protection system?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The second supplementary question: the Minister mentioned about audit agencies and broadening of the audit scope just now, and that MSF will announce the enhanced measures come next year, 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry set up clear timelines, audit and review mechanisms and public reporting expectations for these enhancements, so that agencies are held to consistent standards across, and families can have this confidence and trust, especially in suspected child abuse cases, so that they are not missed or delayed in reporting?

sections.label: Platform establishment and coordination
sections.summary: The Member asks when the platform will be established and what ensures coordination among agencies meanwhile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Minister has mentioned that MSF is working on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask when would this platform be established and in the meantime, in the absence of such a platform, what is being done to ensure coordination among all these agencies?

sections.label: Physical sighting requirement
sections.summary: The Minister confirms physical sighting of the child is the current requirement, not voice or third-party verification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Member asked about the need for physical sighting of the child if there are concerns, the answer is yes, that is the current requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To see the child physically, not just to hear the child's voice or be assured by some third party, including a caregiver, or a Zoom kind of verification.

sections.label: Case leads and safety plans
sections.summary: For tier one and tier two cases, a case lead ensures consistency and centralised decision making, with safety plans and possible removal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And therefore, when they need help, we need to make sure that there is help available, both informal within the family, as well as in the community through social service organisations, community organisations and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But when a case is a high risk, a tier two, or for that matter, a tier one case where the child protection management agencies come in, there are a number of organisations involved and ultimately, there is a case lead for each of these cases, tier two, tier one, so that there is consistency, so that there is a centralised decision making, but in partnership with the other organisations and community groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: When a safety plan is brought in, next of kin may be asked to be involved to keep an eye, sight the child, child stay over with the next of kin, rather than with the parent who may be dealing with issues, or may be a person of concern to the authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There could be more intrusive measures that need to be taken to safekeep the child, including removing the child from parent or parents, and putting them either with next of kin, with foster families or in children's homes, while the issues are being addressed and being worked through.

sections.label: NAVH calls recorded and transcribed
sections.summary: All calls to the NAVH are automatically recorded, logged and transcribed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: All calls to the NAVH are automatically recorded, logged and transcribed.

sections.label: Child death reviews and Protective Service
sections.summary: Each child death brings a review and actions to close gaps, and the Protective Service is now unified with officers specialising in communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: If he is asking about past child deaths, each time there is a child death, there is a review and actions taken to close the gaps, tighten the processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The second question he asked is about specialisation and the Protective Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is now a unified Protective Service, but there are officers who specialise in certain kinds of communities – whether it is children, seniors and so on.

sections.label: SUSS protection specialisation course
sections.summary: SUSS launched its Social Work and Social Development Faculty with a specific specialisation in Protection in its undergraduate course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) which recently launched its Social Work and Social Development Faculty has a specific concentration or specialisation in their undergraduate course on "Protection".

sections.label: Officer caseload reduction target
sections.summary: The Minister said cases per officer fell from 40 to 35, and the member asks whether the Ministry targets a further reduction to 25 or 20.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Foo Cexiang, I know you also filed a Parliamentary Question on this for tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, I remember the Minister mentioned earlier that the number of cases per officer has been reduced from 40 to 35, if I recall correctly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: My question is whether the Ministry has a target to reduce this even further, quite substantively to, for example, 25 or even 20.

sections.label: Officer morale and closing gaps
sections.summary: The member asks how officers' morale will be kept high while gaps that led to the tragedy are closed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: My question to the good Minister and the good Minister of State is how are we going to take care of our diligent, exceptional, dedicated officers who are the vast majority in each of these institutions and have their morale kept high while in parallel, we close the gaps that have led to this tragedy?

sections.label: Technology adoption to enhance processes
sections.summary: The force is looking into adopting technology to enhance processes and procedures, improve efficiency and shorten case closure and resident responses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: One is in terms of the overall technology adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier, we are always, especially as a professional force, eagerly looking into how we can better adopt technology to enhance our processes, our procedures, improve efficiency and in fact, even shorten what we can do to close every single case and to get back to every single resident.

sections.label: Follow-up action and coordination centre
sections.summary: The tech system must flag follow-up action with task owners and supervisor clearance, and the Government is asked how it will measure the coordination centre's success.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The issue in Megan's case was about the follow-up action, so the tech system has to do more than sense make, but also ensure that follow up action is clearly flagged to be done with the clear task owners and requiring supervisor clearance in line with the protocols that are being set up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How will the Government measure the success and effectiveness of this new coordination centre in improving child protection outcomes?

sections.label: Measuring success of coordination tools
sections.summary: Success is measured by sector cohesiveness, coordination, and earlier identification of high-risk cases, and the Police introduced a Family Violence Training Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: How to measure the success of these tools?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I would say, let us look at the overall cohesiveness of the sector, the ability to coordinate the work more effectively, the ability to identify earlier high-risk cases and to intervene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Speaker, earlier in my initial PQ reply, I mentioned that the Police had made several enhancements, one of which was the introduction of the Family Violence Training Package for all frontline and IOs.
